items.title: New Trump tariffs 'make it harder for Australian businesses to compete'
items.description: The Business Council of Australia says a new tariff will make it harder for Australian businesses to compete in the US and could reduce investment.

items.title: Breaking: Reginald Chard, Australia's last surviving Kokoda veteran, dies at 102
items.description: Australia's last surviving Kokoda campaign veteran, Reginald James Chard OAM, has died aged 102.

items.title: Defence minister confirms former senior naval officer faces court martial
items.description: A former senior naval officer will face charges in a military trial set down for up to six weeks from September 14, and a military court has ordered their identity to remain suppressed.

items.title: Four Corners withdraws episodes by sacked reporter
items.description: The ABC has withdrawn the Four Corners programs Meth Highway and Cocaine Nation by sacked reporter Mahmood Fazal due to concerns about accuracy.

items.title: Socceroos star allegedly tests positive for cocaine after speeding
items.description: Police say they stopped the 22-year-old in a BMW Coupe about 1am today and allege he was travelling 109 kilometres per hour on the Anzac Bridge.

items.title: Islanders sang hymns and kept vigil over body of teenager washed ashore
items.description: Twenty-seven people including families with young children went missing after two boats capsized in rough seas in Papua New Guinea's north-east on Saturday.

items.title: Rare eye disorder linked to Ozempic-like medications
items.description: The Therapeutic Goods Administration has issued a safety warning for a rare, but serious risk of vision impairment from taking GLP-1-based drugs such as Ozempic and Wegovy.

items.title: Live: Ponga ruled out of Roosters blockbuster
items.description: Newcastle will be without star fullback Kalyn Ponga for their crucial clash with the high-flying Roosters. Follow live.

items.title: Drivers urged not to panic-buy as fuel price hikes nowhere near record high
items.description: Australians are being urged by a peak motorist association not to panic-buy fuel amid a flare-up of tensions in the Middle East, saying prices are nowhere near April's record high.

items.title: Radical groups have a shared hatred of Jews, royal commission hears
items.description: The chief executive of a foundation combating antisemitism says extremist groups from across the political spectrum are posing an unprecedented threat to Australia's Jewish community.

items.title: Calls for change after French apprentice jockey's track work death
items.description: French apprentice jockey Marina Morel died after a fall during track work at Gulgong. Her family is calling for changes to the way racehorse injuries are managed.

items.title: The Commonwealth Games have never opened like this, but maybe they should
items.description: The 2026 Commonwealth Games are like no other that came before them and the opening ceremony was similarly unique in a way that will make it hard to go back.

items.title: AI has changed what criminals can do with your stolen Origin data
items.description: The theft of names, addresses and phone numbers may seem less serious than stolen bank details, but cyber experts say AI is changing what criminals can do with that information.

items.title: Swimmer praises Rinehart for bonuses amid warning to not thank billionaire
items.description: Swimming star Kyle Chalmers praises billionaire Gina Rinehart over bonuses for Commonwealth Games medals, as a report suggests athletes have been told not to thank the mining magnate.

items.title: Adolescence creator tackles teen rehab very differently in The Good Boy
items.description: Emmy Award-winning Adolescence co-creator Stephen Graham tackles teen delinquency in a very different way in The Good Boy.

items.title: How and how often should you be cleaning out your freezer?
items.description: When it comes to kitchen cleaning, the freezer is the last frontier — a forgotten wasteland where food goes to die. But it's not hard to clean, and there are good reasons to do it.

items.title: Budjerah's debut album Gentleman has been a long time coming
items.description: Two-time ARIA Award-winning music artist Budjerah has just released his long-awaited debut album and announced an official tour.

items.title: Automakers in shock as China takes over
items.description: In June, a bulk carrier made an unprecedented delivery of EVs to Australia, sounding an ominous warning to the world's automakers.

items.title: Warning spy laws too broad and could undermine democracy
items.description: A major review warns parts of Australia's national security laws could undermine democracy and press freedom.

items.title: Zelenskyy just scored an 'own goal' and it cost him big time
items.description: The Ukrainian president's decision to fire his popular, tech-savvy 35-year-old Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov last week baffled many. Analysts say what happens next could be pivotal to the war.

items.title: Aboriginal man died after being handcuffed in Adelaide CBD, police say
items.description: South Australian Police say they will treat an internal investigation into the death of a 23-year-old Aboriginal man in custody with the "utmost importance".

items.title: Child abuse reporting scheme sees hundreds of complaints in first weeks
items.description: The reportable scheme launched July 1, brought forward by 12 months, providing a consistent framework for reporting sexual offences, violence, and neglect.

items.title: Conspiracy theories about AusAlert test spreading online
items.description: From wrapping your phone in foil to secret phones, ABC NEWS Verify takes a look into some of these false claims and real concerns about AusAlert to try to answer a few questions.

items.title: RSPCA investigates deliberate attacks on kangaroos in Albany
items.description: The RSPCA is investigating reports of kangaroos being deliberately run over in Albany, Western Australia.

items.title: Families of Sea World crash victims say 'lives changed forever'
items.description: After the powerful family statements had been read, Coroner Carol Lee teared up as she made her closing address to the court.
